cards.text: Someone appears, marching in from Edom, the people descended from Esau (Genesis 36:9), coming from Bozrah. He's robed in splendor, marching in the greatness of His strength.

cards.question: The One marching in from Edom has stained garments. What color is the stain?

cards.text: Then comes the question: Who is this? Nobody has to introduce Him. He answers for Himself, proclaiming vindication.

cards.question: The One from Edom says He is mighty to save.
Next comes the question of why His clothes are red. They look like the garments of someone who does what?

cards.text: He answers that He has trodden the winepress. Me? I've never stomped ANYTHING, friend, because I don't have feet, I have a gold base and a whole lot of confidence.

cards.question: He says He trod the winepress ___, and no one from the nations was with Him.

cards.text: Then the picture turns, and it isn't grapes anymore. He says He trampled them in His anger and trod them down in His fury.

cards.question: The One from Edom says He trampled and trod down in His fury. What spattered His garments?

cards.text: So why all this? He tells us exactly what was in His heart.

cards.question: He says the day of ___ was in His heart.
Along with the day of vengeance, He says the year of His redemption was still far off.

cards.text: Then He says, "I looked," and you can feel the whole scene go quiet. He's looking around for help.

cards.question: When the One from Edom looked for someone to help, what did He find?
When no one assisted the One from Edom, He says He was relieved.
With no one to help, He says His own ___ brought Him salvation.

cards.text: And He adds, "My own wrath upheld Me." Meanwhile I can't seal ONE cookie box without a baker, which is exactly why you got an invitation, friend.

cards.question: He says the ones He trampled in His anger were the nations.

cards.text: He finishes: "in My wrath I made them drunk and poured out their blood on the ground." No one helped Him, and the One mighty to save did it all with His own arm.

findings.problem: The opening card doesn't give the scene's context. It never says this is Isaiah's prophecy, who the speaker is, or what is going on. It only says 'Someone appears,' so the baker doesn't know whose message this is or where it sits in the book.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Asking the color of the stain is a pure detail guess. Nothing on card 1 lets the baker reason toward crimson over purple or blue. It is the same kind of question as the Psalm 23 'what does He anoint David's head with' bad example.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The rest of the question ('and no one from the nations was with Him') hands the baker the answer 'alone' and rules out 'twice' and 'daily.' The card tests nothing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'With no one to help,' and card 14 has just established that no one helped. Both rule out the wrong answers 'people' and 'servants,' so 'arm' is the only answer left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites only Isaiah 63:6. It also uses verse 5 (no one helped, His own arm) and verse 1 (mighty to save).

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'Did it all with His own arm' stretches verse 5. That verse says His arm brought Him salvation and His wrath upheld Him. It doesn't say He did everything with His arm.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. Papa Dorin is a stamper whose whole job is pressing down, so 'I've never stomped ANYTHING' reads oddly for him. The 'whole lot of confidence' tag doesn't connect to stomping, and a baker would have to puzzle it out.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: Most story cards (1, 3, 8, 10, 13, 19) are plain retelling with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice: no reactions, disbelief, comparisons or loud moments. Only cards 6 and 17 attempt humor, and card 6 doesn't land.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
